# OLYMPUS v0.0.27, "Away the boarding party": the build sheet

Written 2026-11-19 for the round's five implementers (A to E) and the lead, who integrates. It is the contract between roles that build in parallel without talking. It sits on **v0.0.26 "Bang, then go" as integrated** (`.run/v026-design/sheet.md`, §14 the check; the handoffs `.run/v026/{lead,a,b,c,d}.md`; `.run/v026/integrate.md`; the integrator's snapshot `.run/v027/v026-snapshot.tree` **a49eac55** = the v0.0.25 tag 077e4f4 + `.run/v027/v026-snapshot.patch`, 77 files, merged in v0.0.26's order stage 0, D, A, B, C), which itself sits on **v0.0.25 as tagged** (077e4f4; `.run/v025/integrate.md`, `fix.md`). The build starts on v0.0.26's tag (or, until it is cut, on v0.0.25 + that patch, its write-tree checked a49eac55); where the tag differs from what is read here, the code decides, stage 0 says so in `.run/v027/lead.md`, and the roles adapt. **§14 lists every correction this check made.**

It is merged from three lens notes in `.run/v027-design/`: **fight.md** (the defenders, live fire both ways, the fire team, the casualty's care, **FT§n**), **ship.md** (the hauler, the collar and the override, the scene's frame, the look and the costs, **SH§n**) and **carried.md** (what v0.0.25 and v0.0.26 leave open, **CA§n**, items **K1** to **K8**, **I1** to **I5**). Where this sheet is silent, the docs decide: DESIGN.md and the user's rules first, then TECH §1.3, then the sections cited, then the lens notes ("as designed" means their mechanism, constants and tests stand unless this sheet changes them). **Where the lenses disagree, the simpler one wins unless the play needs the other** (the user's rule, below); every such choice is settled in §0. My own choices are marked (my call).

**Lines.** Every name, file and function below was checked on the snapshot a49eac55 (a scratch worktree, removed after; §14). FT read the v026-c worktree, SH the main tree mid-integration, CA v0.0.26's final tree and the v0.0.25 tag; where they differ from the snapshot, §14 says what changed. **Every hunk is named by its function**; a line is only ever a pointer. DF§n is v0.0.26's defenders lens (`.run/v026-design/defenders.md`).

## The release in a page

ROADMAP §4.2's row 0.0.7g, `test-collar` "Away the boarding party" (ROADMAP §19's question 8 by default; COMBAT §14.1 to §14.6 in the scene's slice, §7.11 in free fall, §11's flashbang in a pressurised space; WEAPONS §8, frangible against bulkheads): **the first live fight**. A Belt ice hauler, the *Patient Mule*, coasting at 0 G, its crew struck to the corvette's hail; deck 2 (the berths) did not answer. You are the boarding team's #3, with a fire team of four, through the mated collar's lock on an override; armed men who are not role-players hold the deck and choose by their nerve; rounds are live both ways and wounds are real; the deck is secured, or the party falls back to the lock. The road is the user's: "now to bring this gameplay smoothly to CQB room clearing in full G, then ship CQB in microgravity and grav boots, and to real combat with enemies" (2026-11-08), and the order of 2026-11-17 (0.0.7e, 0.0.7f, then 0.0.7g).

**The one idea** (both play lenses agree; my call): **the house's live lane made real, on a second ship, not a new engine.** It is the shoot house's lane (tower, #2, bundles, T, faults, run sheet, card, bots) on the Wreck's model of a ship (one area, decks, hatches, faces, mag boots, `familiar: 'walls'`), with v0.0.26's defenders who choose, selected by two fields of the operation record: **`R.house.ship = 'hauler'`** (through a registry, so the Wreck's ~55 branches are not doubled) and **`R.house.boarding`** (the fight's record), and one switch: **the live ledger's rule `'real'`**, read through `realOf(state)`. On 'real' a strike is the round's own load on the man's own body (`applyHit`, the bus on), and "down" is the body's own, never paint. On 'wound' and 'count' nothing moves.

**What is new, exactly** (the rest is reuse, §0 item 1's table):
1. **Live rounds both ways**: the marines' frangible, the defenders' ball; the carrier with its plates in; no "Hit!", no paint; the body's knock, down and rise; three ends (secured, fallen back, you down) (B).
2. **A fire team of four**: #1 the team leader and #2 the automatic rifleman hold the lock's end of the passage (a new small brain, `holders.js`); #3 you and #4 your buddy (v0.0.19's #2 as built, labelled "Four") clear the compartments; the leader's bubbles take the instructor's place (C).
3. **A hauler's crew deck**: deck 2 of the *Patient Mule*, the lock, the passage, two cabins and the bunk room, every opening a hatch, as data in the Wreck's model (stage 0's data, D's scene).
4. **Defenders who are not role-players**: pirates or smugglers (COMBAT §14.4's irregulars) and the hauler's own unarmed crew, drawn from the seed; the irregular table with blind fire and flight inside a compartment; the civilians who never fight; the side's give-up on the intercom (A).
5. **Your tourniquet** and the corpsman's card after the fight (B).
6. **Frangible against bulkheads**: every miss meets a face; their ball holes cabin walls, bulkheads and the hull, counted and told; no onward round, no leak (B, D).
7. **The G-11 at 0 G lands where it is thrown**: the first face met and a rebound of at most 1.5 m (B).

**The narrowest fight that plays** (my calls, the lenses': FT§0 item 4, SH§0): **one deck** (§0 item 2); static posts, nobody changes compartment; the holders never leave their posts; no throw, no hand to hand, no hostage at gunpoint; no new gun (the R-7 and P-12 with ball for the defenders); walls stop every round; no leak, no blood globules, no buddy aid.

**Before the roles, stage 0 (the lead)** confirms what v0.0.26 shipped, records every pin, reads the quick suite's CPU on a quiet run (four read-only memos only if it is over), makes the ship seam a registry, lifts v0.0.26's one-scene gate on the defenders' brain to one predicate, lands the seams as stubs and the hauler's deck, its stands and its people as data (unreachable), and moves no tick.

**The roles**: **A** the defenders; **B** live fire and the wound; **C** the fire team; **D** the ship and the scene; **E** the look. **Merge order**: stage 0, B, A, C, D, E (§7).

**Ship rules** (my calls):
- Stage 0 ships when F150 (nothing moves) is green.
- `test-collar` is reachable by URL from D's merge (`menu: false`); it goes on the Tests menu, last, after "Hold to hold" ("Bang, then go" sits after "Stack and clear, live" since v0.0.26's integration), when F150, F153 (no dead end), F155 (hors de combat) and F165 (cost) are green. F167 (balance) is printed: red there is a question for the user with the figures, never a constant tuned (FT§17 risk 3).
- The look ships at each set's default until scored, said in the announcement.
- **The cut line**, if the round must shrink, in this order: (1) the hull's line told (the count stays on the card); (2) the unsealed vac suit (coveralls only); (3) flight (read as a freeze, "no way out"); (4) the holders' fire (they hold, their words bubbles at them; the fight is your pair's); (5) blind fire; (6) the fall back (the scene ends secured or with you down). **Never cut**: real wounds both ways, the doctrine tables, the crew, the side's give-up, the tourniquet, the corpsman's card, the registry, the override, the atlas fix.

**The user's rules over every section**: "keep things simple, it's a game. I love the attention do detail, but only if it won't impact gameplay or performance (or introduce so much complexity it creates bugs)" (2026-11-19); "forget voice synthesis, no voices." (2026-11-19: every line a text bubble at its speaker, the hauler's intercom included); the look chosen from numbered samples the user scores, the rated sets collapsed at the bottom of the gallery (2026-11-19); "we shouldn't know what's behind closed doors or walls without looking" (2026-11-19: `familiar: 'walls'`); "Paintball should end if the hit is 'fatal'" (2026-11-16, which this scene makes real: no paint, the round is the wound); "enemies are NPCs and they run their own procedure to eliminate us ... Suppression, training and exprience will decide how well NPCs can respond to threats and whether they fight back, try to rush for cover or flee all together" (2026-11-07); "Try keeping rifles looking like rifles even zero G stuff, let's say we use footing to hold recoil" (2026-11-08); test scenes explain nothing beyond their goal line (2026-11-06); one quantity, one helper; visuals obey the sim; AZERTY labels on physical codes.

**Kept as built and starred**: "Stack and clear" (★ 2026-11-17) and every pin of v0.0.26 (F150), but for D's one named re-record (K3: `zerocqb-pin`'s seven cells and test-zerocqb's digest, the cause on each line); F1 to F149 never loosened.

**Rules of the round**: as v0.0.26's, with `.run/v027/` for patches and handoffs (it survives a reboot), `/private/tmp/claude-501/olympus-build/v027/<role>/` for scratch, worktrees `git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/v027-<role> v0.0.26` (until the tag is cut: `v0.0.25` with `.run/v027/v026-snapshot.patch` applied, its write-tree checked a49eac55) with `.run/v027/stage0.patch` applied and `node_modules` linked, removed at the end. Five roles at `JOBS=2` each, `JOBS=1` while the user plays (input idle under 5 minutes, not the server alone); heavy suites wait for the lead's quiet run. A quick file under 3 s × k of CPU; **the round's new quick files 8 s in all** (§6). No role commits; the lead integrates and releases.

**Ports**: A 8230, B 8231, C 8232, D 8233, E 8234; reviews 8235 and 8236; the lead 8239; the runner's 8240 to 8249. Kill every server you start.

**Interfaces first**: each role writes §3's exports as stubs, fills them, and tests against its own stub of another role's export until that role merges. Every stub returns today's answer where `R.house.boarding` is absent, so a stubbed role moves nothing.

**Integration**: the stage-0 tree the base; each patch cut against the tree the merges before it left (A on B's, C on A's, D on C's, E on D's), applied with `git apply --3way` in the merge order; after each, `QUICK=1 node tests/run.mjs`, `'env-noregress ›'`, `'ship-seam ›'` and the pins (`house-pin`, `house-live-pin`, `house-pin-drawn`, `zerocqb-pin`, `breach-pin`).

URL `?play=test-collar&tier=…&seed=…&hour=…&holdouts=pirates|smugglers&setup=go|cabin2|fallback` (no `&setup`: the brief, as the house's and the Wreck's; §0 item 14); every house option, `&opfor` and `&loadout` dropped with one toast, "The *Patient Mule* is boarded as set." (`SHIPS.hauler.dropped`, `debug.js shipChoice` reading `rec.ship`). 2. **The override** (D; SH§5). In the lock on locked boots, chambered at the fill (§0 item 11); three brief bubbles at the leader; "Override.": Four at the lock's panel rolls `d20 + Tech` against `OVERRIDE_DC` 13 (10 + 3 × TL 1); 120 s on a pass, +30 s a point under, at most 300 s; a miss by 5 or more locks the panel out once for 60 s more ("Panel's locked me out. Again."). One outcome skip behind one splash ("The lock cycles on the override: 2:30"), never a fast-forward; none is set over a surprise. At its end the holdouts are alerted (A reads the fact `'collar' { phase: 'override', dc, roll, ms, tries }`), the panel's lamp goes green, the inner hatch's dogs come off (`op.js breakOpening`'s undog, the Wreck's). "Stand by." GO.

31. **Stands in the house's form, and only the drawn ones.** `shoothouse.js standsOf` (`leg = Number(stand[0]) - 1`), `two.js legOf`, `opfor.js legIndex` (a man of a leg a setup cleared is ruled out by it) and shoothouse's leg readers (the clear gate, `liveLegEnd`, the move-on) take a man's leg from his stand's first digit, as `wreck.js`' stands are written. The posts' ids SH§3.5 gave (`2a` to `2e`, "deck 2") would have put every holdout on leg 1. The ids, by leg (`HAULER_ORDER`: 1 the passage, 2 cabin 1, 3 the bunk room, 4 cabin 2), each with SH§3.5's point it takes (± 0.3 m, stage 0 settles them on the grid and through `spotCheck`):

| Stand | Leg, room | SH§3.5's | Face | Covers | Drawn |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `1a` | 1, the passage | 2a (11.1, 4.45) behind the DC locker | deck | the lock's hatch, 8.6 m | the barricade: pirates 1 in 2, smugglers 1 in 3 |
| `2a` | 2, cabin 1 | 2b's point (4.9, 0.6), **on the deck** | deck | its hatch | smugglers only (the pirates shut the crew in cabin 1, §9) |
| `3a` | 3, the bunk room | 2d (8.6, 9.0) between two berth boxes | deck | its hatch | either |
| `3b` | 3, the bunk room | 2e (3.9, 6.3) behind the head's stalls | deck | the room's length | either |
| `4a` | 4, cabin 2 | 2c (8.2, 1.3) behind the desk column | deck | its hatch | either |
| `4b` | 4, cabin 2 | **on the deckhead over its hatch** (SH's deckhead man, moved from cabin 1 to cabin 2: §9 item 5, FT's acceptance) | deckhead | its hatch | pirates 1 in 3 |
| `2c`, `2d` | 2, cabin 1 | the crew's corner | deck | | the pirates' two shut-in crewmen |
| `3c`, `3d`, `4c` | 3, 4 | the crew's hiding places | deck | | the smugglers' 2 or 3 unarmed crewmen |

`HAULER_POSTS` holds the armed stands, `HAULER_CREW` the crew's; both are stands of the hauler's spec (`shipSpec('hauler').stands`) with roles in `courses.js HAULER_ROLES` (`standsOf` throws on a stand with no role). The fill keeps the draw's stands only (`R.turners = standsOf(state).filter(s => drawn.has(s.stand))`, v0.0.26's breach filter's form), so no paper board stands aboard. Your #2's cue and the clear gate read the leg as on every lane.

32. **The people** (none of the lenses said who they are): every person of the scene is a generated person (the user, 2026-11-05: "All people generated"), drawn by `people/staff.js drawStaff` from a post in `src/data/people/posts.js`, stage 0's data with the deck: `belt-mule:board-tl` and `belt-mule:board-ar` (Corps, the boarding team's #1 and #2, `unitId` '2/4' as every post), `belt-mule:holdout-1` to `-4` and `belt-mule:crew-1` to `-3`. The posts' ranks come from `data/people/ranks.js RANKS`, which holds the Corps' and the Navy's only: **one row `Civ` ('Civilian', no grade, branch 'civilian', ages 18 to 60, kind 'junior')** for the holdouts and the crew, never shown in a word (my call: the smallest true thing; nothing iterates `RANKS`). If the row moves any pin, they take `Pvt` and the card and plaque never name a rank for them. Your #2 is `drawTwo` as built.

SHIPS = { wreck: { id, area, lane: 'W', decks, trunks, plans, legs, seq, words, roles, staff: 'cadre', tug, setups, dropped },

## 7. Dependencies and the merge order

**Stage 0 needs**: v0.0.26's tag (or v0.0.25 + `.run/v027/v026-snapshot.patch`, a49eac55, until it is cut); v0.0.26's own code for the two saves; DESIGN.md's log.

**B needs**: stage 0's `newLedger(rule)`, `realOf`, `boarding-world`; `penetrate.js` (`WALLS`, `ARMOUR.carrier`), `wounds.js`, `throw.js` as built. B's tests drive its own functions on `boarding-world` and scripted records; nothing of A's, C's or D's (they merge after it).

**A needs**: B's real down and `wouldHave`'s bus (merged first), B's kit ids and `aid.js`; stage 0's `choosesOf`, `fireTeamOf` stub, `HAULER_POSTS`, `HAULER_CREW` through `shipOf(H)`, the posts' people; D's override fact (a stub: alerted at the fill).

**C needs**: A's `liveStateOf` and men (merged), B's `aid.js`; stage 0's `HAULER_HOLDERS`.

**D needs**: A, B and C merged for the bots and the sweep, A's `protectedOf` for the 'protected' fault and its case; stage 0's registry, deck, stands, roles and posts; E's nothing (defaults draw as built).

**E needs**: the stage-0 tree for the samples on day 1; A's 'blind' and 'flee' states and D's scene for `ui-collar` (E merges last); the user's scores (each default stands).

**Merge order: stage 0, B, A, C, D, E** (my call; each layer on the one it reads). B to C move no pinned cell (every guard on 'real' or `R.house.boarding`); D moves `zerocqb-pin` by K3 only, its own step, each cell's cause in its handoff; E is render only and moves no sim pin.

## 9. Acceptance: what the user must feel

The default: the sergeant by T, pirates drawn (four armed: the barricade `1a`, the bunk room's `3a` and `3b`, cabin 2's deckhead man `4b`; two of the hauler's crew shut in cabin 1, `2c` and `2d`), the barricade drawn.

1. **0:00, the lock.** Four marines on locked boots in the lock's dim; three bubbles at the leader: "*Patient Mule*, Belt ice hauler. The crew struck to the hail and are on deck one. Deck two did not answer: armed men, and some of the crew. The crew are not targets." "Frangible. Feet on the plate." "Four, override." The splash, "The lock cycles on the override: 2:30". The panel goes green.
2. **0:30, the passage.** "Stand by." GO. The leader and the AR go through, the AR planting on the deckhead; "Set." The barricade man behind the damage-control locker 8.6 m down fires a pair: it cracks past you in the hatch (your felt jumps); "Contact forward!" The AR's pair; the pirate drops into cover and **fires blind** over the locker, rounds slapping the bulkheads by the lock, one into the hull: "Hull's holed. Keep going." T: "Firing blind. Get on him." You may join, or wait: the holders' fight.
3. **1:00, cabin 1.** "Three, Four: cabin one. Go." You and Four stack on its hatch on your boots, Four close behind you and in on your cue. Dark until you look: two men COWERING in the corner, no guns. "He's crew. Challenge him." "Show me your hands!": both give. A round at them is the card's worst line.
4. **1:40, the bunk room: the bang.** "Flash it": the G-11 goes straight through the hatch, slaps the far bulkhead and bangs in the room. A pirate DAZED, a hand to his eyes; you in on the bang ("ON THE BANG 1.2 S"), your corner, the pair: **he sags from his boots and does not move**; no "Hit!", no paint, a casualty. The second, facing away, deaf, not blind: suppressed, his nerve misses, a push-off behind the berth boxes 2 s across the open, or blind fire. Four's pair. "Clear!"
5. **2:40, cabin 2: the hard one.** A pirate on the deckhead over the hatch; he is first: one round on your plate (a thump), one in your left arm. **You are down**, hanging from your boots, 15 to 25 s, the screen your own; Four "Covering!", his pair, the man down. "On your feet." "Bleeding hard from the left arm: a tourniquet, now." 25 s in parts; your rifle hand now −6, and the card will say so.
6. **3:40, the give-up.** Three of four down: the roll at 50%. A bubble at the bunk room's speaker: "We give up! Don't shoot! We're coming out!" The barricade man comes out from the locker, hands up; Challenge. "Deck secure."
7. **4:00, the card.** THE *PATIENT MULE* · BELT ICE HAULER · DECK 2 · SECURED 3:58 · OURS: YOU, A GUNSHOT WOUND IN THE LEFT ARM, TOURNIQUET AT 3:02, STABLE · THEIRS: 3 DOWN (1 DIED OF WOUNDS BEFORE THE AID STATION), 1 GAVE UP · THE CREW: 2, UNHURT · YOUR ROUNDS 11, THROUGH A BULKHEAD 0 · THEIRS 23, HOLES 5, THE HULL HOLED 2 · THEIR CHOICES (a line a man) · FIRED FLOATING: NONE. "Again", "Again as …", "Another hauler".
8. **Lower and higher.** The recruit by the keys is slower at every hatch, hit more often, and on some seeds two marines fall: "Fall back to the lock!", "Back to the lock", the splash, FELL BACK WITH 2 CASUALTIES. The tier one by T clears it in about two and a half minutes and is seldom touched. Smugglers with pistols: a knock of seconds, never through your plates.
9. **The look**: the Belter deck, the holdouts' dress, blind fire and a man down at 0 G as you scored them, or the defaults, named.
10. **Carried**: your #2 in on his cue through the Wreck's hatches too.

**For the integrator** (as v0.0.26's): F150 after stage 0 and each merge; `QUICK=1 node tests/run.mjs` after each; the gauges never loosened (`'house-flawless-quick ›'`, `'house-flawless-keys ›'` all MET); `game-upgrade` loads every save to v0.0.26's and the two new ones; F60, F148 and F165 and `?bench=collar` PASS on a quiet machine, the user judging Windows; a browser smoke on :8239 (`?play=test-collar&tier=private` by the keys to the card; `&tier=sgt&holdouts=smugglers` by T; `&setup=fallback` on another seed; no page error, console error or failed request; the server killed after); the heavy suites once on a quiet machine after the last merge (`env-noregress`, `collar-nodead`, `collar-balance`, `collar-pin`, `collar-tick`, `collar-again`, `ui-collar`, the house pins, `zerocqb-pin`, `breach-pin`, `house-flawless-live`, v0.0.26's heavy suites); `house-done` with every row F1 to F169.

## 11. Risks (each owned)

1. **The registry moves a Wreck pin** (stage 0): one of the 59 `'wreck'` literals (and the two `wreckDeckAt` imports) read wrong. `zerocqb-pin`'s quick cell, test-zerocqb's digest and the source scan; done first, alone.
2. **'real' leaks into the live lane** (B, A): every guard reads `realOf`; `house-live-pin` and `breach-pin` after each merge (F150).
3. **The knock takes the game away** (B): 15 to 25 s on your back a wound (FT§2). If the user finds it long, the one switch is a scene's knock factor on the player (question 5); `TRAINED_K` is the body's for everyone and is not touched.
4. **The holders win the fight alone** (C): `collar-team` prints the barricade man's down time; if the passage is always clear before cabin 1, the barricade's weight drops (one table).
5. **The rise** (A): a man knocked by an arm wound rising after "Clear!" reopens the room (the house's rule as built); `collar-nodead` prints it; if it dead-ends a lane, a man down at his compartment's "Clear!" and covered stays down for the scene (one condition).
6. **Balance unknown before the build** (the lead): F167 stated; red is a question with the figures.
7. **The tick** (every role, D measures): 10 men against the live lane's 4; C's replan rule first, then A's 10 Hz brain (§0 item 13), then the armed cap to 3. Never a brain simplified first.
8. **The atlas** (E): the sealed suit's pixels may read the skin; then `RIFLE_SLOTS_MIN` 8, `figures-arms` re-pinned with its cause, the bay at 23:00 measured before it ships.
9. **A crowded passage** (D): the holders, cabin 1's stack and the lock's hatch within 2 m of each other in a 1.5 m passage; the holders' posts 0.9 m from every stack point (`hauler-plans`), else cabin 1 is entered after the bunk room (one table, `HAULER_ORDER`).
10. **The 2.4 m deckhead** (E, D): a 2.2 literal left in a reader (`render/range.js` defaults 2.2 when a room names none) draws a man on the deckhead 0.2 m off; `ui-collar` shoots the deckhead man.
11. **K3 moves the Wreck's pin** (D): the re-record is its own step with each cell's cause; any other cell that moves stops the merge.
12. **The quick budget** (every role): 8 s; the lead prints each file's CPU at each merge.
13. **Two bodies on a face** (E): the deckhead man over cabin 2's hatch read from above; `wreck-faces` K governs; if he cannot be read, his weight goes to 0 (one table).
14. **A new instinct line stalls the bots** (A, B, C, D): an urgent line with no act leads T's pick and the honest and T bots read it as nothing to press (v0.0.26: `cqb-rp-dazed`, added to `tests/bots/house.mjs` by B after A's warning); D adds the round's (`cqb-rp-blind`, `cqb-rp-flee`, `cqb-passage`) to `SHOT_LINES` and `PAIR_LINES` before its sweep, and each role names any other line it adds in its handoff.
15. **A stand named off the house's form** (stage 0, D): a holdout on the wrong leg is ruled out by a setup, owned by the wrong marine and missed by the clear gate; `hauler-place` refuses any stand whose first digit is not its leg's.

## 13. Open questions for the user, each built with its default

1. **The hull**: a Belt ice hauler, the *Patient Mule*, its crew struck to the hail, armed men and some crew left on deck 2 (or LONGHAUL's small Belt tramp, its whole crew aboard)? *Default: the ice hauler.*
2. **One deck this round** (the passage, two cabins, the bunk room; 3 to 6 minutes), deck 3 through the trunk next round? *Default: one deck.*
3. **Real wounds both ways**: no paint, no "Hit!"; a pair from you ends a man nine times in ten, one round puts him down about a minute; their rounds mostly cost you a knock behind your plates? *Default: yes.*
4. **Plates in for the boarding**: a smuggler's pistol never through your torso, a pirate's rifle about one round in two? *Default: yes.*
5. **Down when hit**, 15 to 25 s on your boots, Four covering, then "On your feet."? *Default: yes, BODY's knock.*
6. **The fire team**: the leader and the AR hold the passage, you and Four clear, the leader's words in place of the instructor's, nobody bounds? *Default: yes.*
7. **Pirates or smugglers, drawn 1 : 1**, the hauler's crew aboard, unarmed, never targets? *Default: yes.*
8. **Their guns**: the R-7 and the P-12 with ball this round, the Belt's TMW-6 with its sample later? *Default: yes.*
9. **Blind fire and flight inside a compartment** for the irregulars? *Default: yes.*
10. **The side gives up at 35% standing, 50% a minute**, on the hauler's intercom? *Default: yes.*
11. **Fall back at two of four down**: walk to the lock, a 30 s splash, the hatch dogged behind you, casualties carried (said, not played)? *Default: yes.*
12. **A round at a man down, hands up or unarmed is a fault**, a cowering or fleeing armed man is not? *Default: yes.*
13. **Walls stop every round**; their ball holes walls and the hull, told and counted, no leak; your frangible turns to dust; through-wall fire later? *Default: yes.*
14. **Your tourniquet**: one row, 25 s in parts, your hand −6 after; no other aid until the corpsman, ours first? *Default: yes.*
15. **The breach by override**: Four's Tech roll, 2 to 5 minutes behind one splash, the holdouts warned by their panel (or a cutting charge, 40 s, loud)? *Default: the override.*
16. **A real deck**: chambered from the start, no UNLOAD, no SHOW CLEAR, no par tones, the card's times kept; every opening a hatch, undogged when the crew struck; the passage 1.5 m and 2.4 m clear? *Default: yes.*
17. **The look**: score `hauler-deck`, `belt-crew` and `board-poses`. *Default: I-a, D-c, B-a, Z-a.*
18. **Where it sits on the Tests menu**: last, after "Hold to hold", the two ships together (or after "Bang, then go", the live scenes together)? *Default: last.*
